L8: Rubin (Robert) Schatten (1911-1977)
L9: Abstract. Rubin (Robert) Schatten was a Polish-American mathe-
L10: matician, working mainly in functional analysis. In the years 1929-
L11: 1933 he studied at the Jan Kazimierz University in Lwów, and a mas-
L12: ter degree has been written under supervision of Stefan Banach. From
L13: September 1936 until his death in August 1977 he stayed in the USA,
L14: where he obtained his doctorate in 1943 and worked at several Amer-
L15: ican universities. Schatten has published 13 scientific papers and two
L16: monographs on operator theory. He was one of the pioneers of the
L17: systematic study of tensor products of Banach spaces. His name in
L18: mathematics was immortalized in Schatten’s classes of operators. We
L19: became interested in Schatten because of the beginnings of his career
L20: in Lwów and the lack of a photo in all descriptions of him. Therefore,
L21: we present the course of his life. His photo will also appear for the first
L22: time.
L23: 2020 MSC:
L24: 01A60, 01A70, 01A73.
L25: Key words and phrases: History of mathematics and mathematicians,
L26: Robert Schatten, functional analysis, tensor product, Schatten classes.
L27: 1.
L28: Biography.
L29: Rubin Schatten was born on 28 January 1911
L30: in Lwów (then it was a Polish city under Austrian rule, now Lviv in
L31: Ukraine). The parents were Józef Saul Schatten (born on 28 March
L32: 1880 in Lwów, son of the merchant Samuel Schatten and Tradala n´ee
L33: Rad) and Osne Laja Schatten n´ee Sieder (born on 14 July 1885 in
L34: Niżankowice, a town 13 km south of Przemyśl, today in Ukraine, as
L35: the daughter of Chana Sieder and the talmudist Mojżesz Judy Sieder,
L36: a merchant and private teacher), who were married on 11 March 1910
L37: in Lwów. At the time of Rubin’s birth, the Schattens lived on Lwia
L38: Street No. 2. Information about the beginnings of Schatten’s life comes
L39: from [Sc18]. We have not been able to establish anything more about
L40: his family, for example, we do not know if he had siblings. From 1942
L41: he used the name Robert.
L42: 164
L43: Rubin (Robert) Schatten (1911-1977)
L44: He graduated from the Private Male Humanistic Gymnasium of the
L45: Jewish People’s and Secondary School Society in Lwów, receiving his
L46: matriculation certificate on 18 June 1929. In September 1929 he began
L47: studying at the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences at Jan
L48: Kazimierz University in Lwów (UJK). His index number was 22362.
L49: The photo of the first page of his entry card is presented on Fig. 1.
L50: Fig. 1. Photo of the first page of Rubin Schatten’s entry card for the first
L51: year of studies at the Jan Kazimierz University, September 26, 1929. Photo
L52: from [Sc5]
L53: At that time, Schatten lived with his parents in the center of Lwów
L54: at Blacharska street 22, he was of Jewish faith, his mother tongue was
L55: Polish, and he had Polish citizenship (see [Sc4]).
L56: In the period 1930–1931 R. Schatten was a board member of the
L57: Society of Jewish Students of Philosophy of Jan Kazimierz University in
L58: Lwów (see [Sc13, p. 23]). The curator of the Society in the years 1924–
L59: 1939 was Prof. Hugo Steinhaus, who was also a supporting member of
L60: the Society.

L116: In 1933, Rubin Schatten wrote his master’s thesis Przestrzenie ab-
L117: strakcyjne [Abstract spaces] under the supervision of Stefan Banach (see
L118: Fig. 3). He submitted it for evaluation on 2 November 1933.
L119: At the beginning of the twentieth century, several non-equivalent
L120: definitions of abstract spaces were given. Many of them were very suc-
L121: cessful, let us mention only: metric spaces (Fr´echet 1906), Hausdorff
L122: topological spaces (Hausdorff 1914), axiomatics of general topological
L123: spaces (Kuratowski 1922).
L124: In the introduction (see Fig. 4) to the master thesis by Schatten [S1]
L125: we read that the aim of the work was to provide theories of the simplest
L126: of abstract spaces by an appropriate selection of axioms, i.e., a set of any
L127: elements to which certain assumptions (certainties) are given. Schatten

L608: In a report [S14], published in 1962, Schatten considered a com-
L609: pletely continuous operators on a complex Hilbert space H. He proved
L610: that every operator in the trace-class is necessarily in the Schmidt-class
L611: and every operator in the Schmidt-class is completely continuous
L612: In a paper [S15], published in 1964, Schatten showed possibility to
L613: consider the concept of a trace-class of operators on general Banach
L614: spaces. He also proved some results for such operators.
L615: In Schatten’s last paper [S16] we have an elementary expository dis-
L616: cussion of the Schauder basis problem and the approximation problem in
L617: Banach spaces. The paper was received by the editors on 15 March 1973
L618: and was dedicated to Professor Beniamino Segre8 for his 70th birthday.
L619: If a Banach space has a Schauder basis then it has the approximation
L620: property, but Per Enflo constructed a Banach space without the approx-
L621: imation property and published it in 1973 in [9]. Schatten was unaware
L622: of the existence of this counterexample.

L641: 8Beniamino Segre (1903–1977), Italian mathematician. He was born and studied
L642: in Turin. He was a professor at the University of Bologna (1931–1938 and 1946–
L643: 1973). In 1938, he lost his professorship as a result of the anti-Jewish laws enacted
L644: under the rule of Benito Mussolini.
L645: He spent the next 8 years in Great Britain
L646: (mainly at the University of Manchester). He is known as one of the main algebraic
L647: geometers of the first half of the 20th century and one of the founders of finite
L648: geometry.
